messages:
katie (support): Hey team — customer Raj (Acme Retail) reporting high latency and 403s. They say traffic from their on‑prem NAT is egressing via our eu-hub proxy instead of us-west, causing auth tokens to be rejected. Any quick ideas? :thinking_face:
raj (customer): seeing 200ms RTT -> 700ms for some requests. Auth sometimes fails with "invalid_aud" and backend logs show X-Region: eu-west-1.
ashwin (eng-net): thanks for the report, Raj — can you paste a curl we can run? also which peering/VPC ID?
katie (support): customer provided this minimal repro:
```
curl -v https://api.redwood.example.com/generate \ 
  -H "Authorization: Bearer <token>" \ 
  -H "X-Customer-Id: acme-retail" \ 
  --resolve api.redwood.example.com:443:198.51.100.22
```
raj (customer): peering: pcx-0a1b2c3d, onprem NAT IP: 198.51.100.22. Token works if we proxy from usw-bastion.
caroline (sre): quick checks: 1) SNAT pool mapping can change region if source IP hash maps to eu hub, 2) proxy stickiness might be keyed on srcIP:port, 3) health-check failover could be bouncing them.
ashwin (eng-net): can we see the customer SNAT mapping in the hub's NAT table? ask Raj to run tcpdump on their NAT for outbound TCP conn to 443 and show source port mapping.
katie (support): Raj sent a capture snippet (redacted):
```
> 198.51.100.22:54321 -> 34.198.10.5:443 (SYN)
> SNAT -> 52.17.88.12:54321 (via eu-hub)
```
caroline (sre): aha — their public IP is being rewritten to 52.17.88.12 which belongs to eu-hub. That explains X-Region header. Why would that NAT mapping pick eu hub?
nashwin (eng-net): two suspects: 1) route-preference ordering in peering — longest prefix or route metrics selecting eu peer, 2) egress proxy affinity table has stale entries mapping that source IP -> eu proxy.
nashwin (eng-net): can we get the NAT translation table for pcx-0a1b2c3d? opsbot, run nat:lookup pcx-0a1b2c3d 198.51.100.22
opsbot: nat:lookup pcx-0a1b2c3d 198.51.100.22 -> result: snat:52.17.88.12:54321, last_seen: 2026-02-14T18:02:12Z, assigned_hub: eu-hub-1
katie (support): is last_seen recent? Raj's capture was within last 5 minutes.
caroline (sre): check health checks for us-west proxy — if us-west proxy had intermittent failures, affinity may fail over to eu. Also check peer BGP flaps.
nashwin (eng-net): I queried route view: peering route preference shows both hubs with equal preference; selection falls back to consistent hashing on session tuple -> their source port 54321 currently hashes to eu-hub. That is deterministic.
nashwin (eng-net): possible mitigations: 1) rotate SNAT port -> different hash -> map to us-west, 2) add srcip prefix override for that customer in route-policy to prefer us-west, 3) fix proxy health so it doesn't evict affinity.
raj (customer): quick test: I restarted NAT and got new src port 54328 — now tests go to us-west and latency drops to 80ms. But we need long term fix.
katie (support): thanks Raj — can you confirm if this change affected billing? we saw token decode 403s earlier.
raj (customer): no billing change, just auth aud mismatch because token audience bound to us-west issuer.
caroline (sre): plan: short-term doc with repro + workaround (rotate NAT port or restart NAT) + apply customer route-policy. Long-term: we should make egress hashing include destination region preference or advertise preferred path via BGP community.
nashwin (eng-net): I'll open a network ops ticket to add a per-customer policy and audit other pcx peerings for equal preference. Ticket: NET-4782.
katie (support): I'll send Raj the workaround steps and ETA. Raj — we'll loop you in on NET-4782. Sorry for the hit — appreciate the quick repro. :handshake:
raj (customer): thanks, appreciate the fast triage.
caroline (sre): note for runbook: add a troubleshooting checklist: traceroute + tcpdump to check SNAT mapping, opsbot nat:lookup, check proxy affinity TTL, and token issuer mapping. Example traceroute command to include: 
```
traceroute -n api.redwood.example.com
```
caroline (sre): closing notes: this is not a NAT bug per se — it's by‑design consistent hashing on SNAT tuple that can cause cross-region egress for some source ports. We should document and add an opt-in override for enterprise VPCs.
opsbot: ticket NET-4782 created -> linked to this thread
katie (support): resolved for customer with workaround; assigning to eng-net for policy change. :white_check_mark:
